summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted for elevated amylase and lipase levels, initially without abdominal pain but with bloating and increased diarrhea. A CT scan showed no structural abnormalities in the transplanted organs, but a subsequent biopsy confirmed mild acute cellular rejection of the pancreatic transplant. She was treated with intravenous steroids and anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG), with adjustment of immunosuppressive therapy including increased tacrolimus and initiation of valganciclovir for prophylaxis. Her pancreatic enzyme levels improved significantly. Due to ATG-related leukopenia, the final dose was reduced. Blood pressure was managed with increased doxazosin, and gabapentin was restarted for phantom limb pain. She was discharged home with close follow-up, new medication instructions, and outpatient lab monitoring.
problems: Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
